learningObjectives: Apply design thinking stages to a real-world design problem.
Convert user research findings into a clearly defined problem statement.
Create focused how-might-we questions for ideation.

activities.title: Design Thinking Map
activities.instruction: Explore how each design thinking stage connects.

content.concept: Design thinking uses empathy, definition, ideation, prototyping, and testing to solve user-centered problems iteratively.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Problem Statement Builder
activities.instruction: Build a focused user problem statement.

content.concept: A strong problem statement identifies the target user, their need, and the meaningful problem without prescribing a solution.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: How Might We Lab
activities.instruction: Transform user problems into design questions.

content.concept: How-might-we questions reframe user problems as open opportunities for generating multiple possible solutions.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Problem Validation
activities.instruction: Select the problem statement supported by evidence.

content.concept: A well-defined problem should connect directly to research evidence and a meaningful user need.
